title: 1999 AMC 8 Problem 23
statement: Square \(ABCD\) has sides of length \(3.\) Segments \(CM\) and \(CN\) divide the square’s area into three equal parts. How long is segment \(CM?\)

solutions.text:
The area of the square is \(3^2 = 9,\) which means that the area of one region is \(9 \div 3 = 3.\)

This means the area of \(\triangle BMC\) is \(3,\) which means that \[ \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot 3 \cdot BM = 3 \]\[ BM = 2. \]

Since \(\triangle BMC\) is right, we have \[ CM = \sqrt{2^2 + 3^2} = \sqrt{13}. \]

Thus, C is the correct answer.
hints: Each of the three regions has area one-third of the square
Use the area of \(\triangle BMC\) to find \(BM\)
